subject: Chemistry
topic: Biomolecules — carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, nucleic acids and hormones.
question: Which of the following statements about monosaccharides is incorrect?
option1: All monosaccharides, including ketoses such as fructose, are reducing sugars.
option2: A monosaccharide cannot be hydrolysed further to give a simpler polyhydroxy aldehyde or ketone.
option3: 2-Deoxyribose is not a monosaccharide because it does not fit the general formula C$_n$(H$_2$O)$_n$.
option4: In sucrose, the fructose unit is present as a five-membered (furanose) ring.
correct_option: 2-Deoxyribose is not a monosaccharide because it does not fit the general formula C$_n$(H$_2$O)$_n$.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Biomolecules — carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, nucleic acids and hormones.
question: Which of the following sets contains only reducing sugars?
option1: Sucrose, maltose and glucose
option2: Lactose, sucrose and galactose
option3: Starch, maltose and fructose
option4: Maltose, lactose and fructose
correct_option: Maltose, lactose and fructose

subject: Chemistry
topic: Biomolecules — carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, nucleic acids and hormones.
question: Which option correctly gives two main functions of carbohydrates in plants?
option1: Glycogen acts as the storage polysaccharide and chitin forms the cell wall.
option2: Cellulose forms the cell wall (structural material) and starch acts as the storage polysaccharide.
option3: Starch forms the cell wall and cellulose acts as the storage polysaccharide.
option4: Glycogen forms the cell wall and sucrose is the main structural material.
correct_option: Cellulose forms the cell wall (structural material) and starch acts as the storage polysaccharide.

option3: 4 and 2
option4: 2 and 4

option2: C1 of $\alpha$-D-glucose and C2 of $\beta$-D-fructose
option3: C1 of $\beta$-D-glucose and C2 of $\alpha$-D-fructose
option4: C1 of $\alpha$-D-glucose and C1 of $\beta$-D-fructose

option1: contains $\beta$-1,4 glycosidic linkages instead of $\alpha$-1,4 linkages
option2: is a linear polymer without any C1–C6 branching
option3: is made of D-fructose units instead of D-glucose units
option4: is even more highly branched than amylopectin

topic: Biomolecules — carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, nucleic acids and hormones.
question: The hydrolysis products of (i) sucrose and (ii) lactose respectively are

option2: (i) $\alpha$-D-glucose + $\beta$-D-fructose; (ii) $\alpha$-D-glucose + $\alpha$-D-glucose
option3: (i) $\beta$-D-glucose + $\alpha$-D-fructose; (ii) $\beta$-D-galactose + $\beta$-D-fructose
option4: (i) D-glucose + D-galactose; (ii) D-glucose + D-fructose
correct_option: (i) $\alpha$-D-glucose + $\beta$-D-fructose; (ii) $\beta$-D-galactose + $\beta$-D-glucose

subject: Chemistry
topic: Biomolecules — carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, nucleic acids and hormones.
question: The basic structural difference between starch and cellulose is that
option1: starch is made of $\beta$-D-glucose units, while cellulose is made of $\alpha$-D-glucose units
option2: starch is made of $\alpha$-D-glucose units (with C1–C6 branching in amylopectin), while cellulose is a straight chain of $\beta$-D-glucose units joined by C1–C4 $\beta$-glycosidic linkages
option3: starch is a linear polymer, while cellulose is highly branched through C1–C6 linkages
option4: starch contains D-fructose units, while cellulose contains only D-glucose units
correct_option: starch is made of $\alpha$-D-glucose units (with C1–C6 branching in amylopectin), while cellulose is a straight chain of $\beta$-D-glucose units joined by C1–C4 $\beta$-glycosidic linkages

question: Which of the following observations CAN be explained by the open chain structure of D-glucose?

option2: Glucose does not give Schiff's test.
option3: Glucose pentaacetate does not react with hydroxylamine.
option4: Glucose exists in two crystalline forms with melting points 419 K and 423 K.
correct_option: Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime.

question: Which of the following sets contains only essential amino acids?
option1: Valine, leucine, isoleucine and lysine
option2: Glycine, alanine, valine and serine
option3: Lysine, tyrosine, proline and glutamic acid
option4: Glutamine, aspartic acid, cysteine and threonine
correct_option: Valine, leucine, isoleucine and lysine

subject: Chemistry
topic: Biomolecules — carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, nucleic acids and hormones.
question: Which of the following statements related to proteins is incorrect?
option1: A peptide linkage (–CO–NH–) is formed between the –COOH group of one amino acid and the –NH$_2$ group of another with loss of water.
option2: The primary structure is the specific sequence of amino acids; any change in it creates a different protein.
option3: During denaturation the primary structure is destroyed, while the secondary and tertiary structures remain intact.
option4: Coagulation of egg white on boiling is an example of denaturation.
correct_option: During denaturation the primary structure is destroyed, while the secondary and tertiary structures remain intact.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Biomolecules — carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, nucleic acids and hormones.
question: Which of the following statements about the secondary structure of proteins is correct?
option1: The $\alpha$-helix is a left-handed screw formed by twisting of the polypeptide chain.
option2: In the $\beta$-pleated sheet, peptide chains are stretched out to nearly maximum extension and laid side by side, held together by intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
option3: The $\alpha$-helix is stabilised mainly by disulphide linkages.
option4: The two common types of secondary structure are the double helix and the triple helix.
correct_option: In the $\beta$-pleated sheet, peptide chains are stretched out to nearly maximum extension and laid side by side, held together by intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Biomolecules — carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, nucleic acids and hormones.
question: The $\alpha$-helix structure of proteins is stabilised by
option1: intermolecular hydrogen bonds between two different polypeptide chains
option2: disulphide bonds between cysteine residues of the same chain
option3: ionic interactions between acidic and basic side chains
option4: intramolecular hydrogen bonds between the N–H group of each amino acid residue and the C=O group of an adjacent turn of the helix
correct_option: intramolecular hydrogen bonds between the N–H group of each amino acid residue and the C=O group of an adjacent turn of the helix

subject: Chemistry
topic: Biomolecules — carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, nucleic acids and hormones.
question: Which of the following is correctly matched?
option1: Myosin – fibrous protein; polypeptide chains run parallel and are held by hydrogen and disulphide bonds
option2: Keratin – globular protein; soluble in water
option3: Insulin – fibrous protein; insoluble in water
option4: Albumin – fibrous protein; chains held side by side
correct_option: Myosin – fibrous protein; polypeptide chains run parallel and are held by hydrogen and disulphide bonds

subject: Chemistry
